route: route 1 (published per-item M/SD, postprint Table 1, exploratory subsample) + route 9 (raw-label vs live-integer response-frequency matching)
evidence: Route 1 (published per-item descriptive statistics), item axis, plus route 9 (response-frequency matching), resp axis. ROUTE 1: the postprint's Table 1 publishes M (SD) per numbered item for the EXPLORATORY sample, so the comparison is run on the 416 live respondents the study flagged Used_Time1_EFA==1 (participants 1-417 except 397; id in the IRW table is the workbook's Participant number). For 36 of the 37 items the live (M,SD) sits within 0.0139 of its OWN published pair AND that pair is the NEAREST of all 37 published pairs -- e.g. T1_OFAQ_16 pub 3.29/0.97 vs obs 3.291/0.969 (d=0.0012, runner-up T1_OFAQ_28 at 0.1124), T1_OFAQ_29 pub 1.88/0.78 vs obs 1.889/0.784 (d=0.0101), T1_OFAQ_8 pub 3.06/1.26 vs obs 3.072/1.253 (d=0.0139, the worst), T1_OFAQ_35 pub 2.82/1.28 vs obs 2.817/1.282 (d=0.0034). Every one of the 36 runner-up distances is at least 2.4x the own-distance. Because the assignment is a bijection over 37 codes and 36 codes each uniquely claim themselves, item 37 is pinned as the residue; its published mean (2.82) is a misprint repeating item 35's printed mean (observed 2.276) while its published SD 1.12 reproduces at 1.123. On the pooled 802-respondent table the same test misassigns 19 of 37, which is a sample-scope artifact (pooled means run 0.01-0.19 higher), not a mapping failure -- hence the subsample. Corroborating and independent of the statistics: the study's own analysis script OFAQR.R assigns T1_OFAQ_k to the same one of the three factors that the OSF scale document assigns statement #k, for all 37. ROUTE 9: the raw OSF workbook stores label strings while the IRW table stores 1..5; all 185 item x level counts match exactly (e.g. T1_OFAQ_1 32/160/165/359/86 raw vs 32/160/165/359/86 live; T1_OFAQ_37 174/298/142/153/35 vs 174/298/142/153/35), confirming 1=Strongly Disagree .. 5=Strongly Agree rather than the reverse or any permuted level. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: route 1 pins each code to a NUMBER in the study's own item list; it cannot detect an error inside that list (if the postprint table and the administered questionnaire agreed on the wrong statement for a number, this route would not see it). It also does not adjudicate the three wording differences between the administered form and the scale document (items 18, 33, 35) -- that choice is documentary, recorded in provenance. See verify_offlinefriend_ofaq.R (VERDICT: PASS).

route: route 5 (subscale/block correlation structure vs MPsychoR ASTI reference, all 5040 permutations) + route 1 (item endorsement order)
evidence: Route 5 (block/subscale structure) run WITHIN the subscale against an external reference matrix, plus route 1 as a corroborating check. Reference = the ASTI dataset in CRAN MPsychoR (n=1,215; 1,129 complete on the ST block), whose 7x7 ST inter-item correlations reproduce Koller et al. (2017) Appendix/DataSheet1.docx to 2dp (e.g. ASTI2-ASTI7 .65/.65, ASTI24-ASTI25 .369/.37, ASTI13-ASTI25 .194/.20). Live data = the study's own OSF CSV, whose ST_1..ST_7 columns are what data/pellerin2020_covid_resources.py melts (n=1,010 per item, matching irw_table_sets). Scoring all 5040 permutations by the Pearson correlation between the 21 off-diagonal reference and live correlations, the SHIPPED mapping (ST_k = k-th ASTI ST item: ASTI2,4,7,13,16,24,25) ranks 1 of 5040, r=0.8987 (Spearman rho=0.8519, also rank 1). Marker facts: the largest of the 21 reference correlations is ASTI2-ASTI7 = .65 and the largest of the 21 live ones is ST_1-ST_3 = .76; the second-tier pair is ASTI24-ASTI25 = .37 / ST_6-ST_7 = .57; ASTI13 is the reference's least-connected ST item (mean r .106) whose single strongest ST partner is ASTI25 (.194), and ST_4 is the live one (mean r .324) whose single strongest partner is ST_7 (.41). Corroborating route 1: in the reference sample ASTI4 is endorsed above ASTI16 (mean 1.72 vs 1.58 on 0-3) and live ST_2 sits above ST_5 (5.043 vs 4.924 on 1-7), the same direction. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the permutations ranked 2-4 are exactly the shipped one with ST_1<->ST_3 swapped (r=0.8962), ST_2<->ST_5 swapped (r=0.8912) and both swapped (r=0.8904) -- all within 0.009 -- so the route pins the BLOCKS {ST_1,ST_3}={ASTI2,ASTI7} and {ST_2,ST_5}={ASTI4,ASTI16} and fixes ST_4=ASTI13, ST_6=ASTI24, ST_7=ASTI25 (swapping 6 and 7 costs 0.039 in r), but it does NOT distinguish ASTI2 from ASTI7 or ASTI4 from ASTI16. Those two assignments rest on presentation order alone; item means do not break either tie (ST_1 5.205 vs ST_3 5.228, a 0.02 gap, and in the reference ASTI2 1.69 vs ASTI7 1.47 runs the other way). Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.
